A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tucker decomposition and selective fine-tuning framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation experiments, F1 scores, computational comparisons, and ablations across five time-series benchmarks, including one-to-one and many-to-one evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds source-loss recovery measurements and experiments comparing frozen-factor PEFT variants with standard PEFT and SFT.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains HOOI-based Tucker decomposition, 2–3 epochs of source recovery training, and core-only target adaptation. Appendix A.8 documents existing adaptation objectives; the new frozen-factor variants are comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SSC, MFD, HHAR, WISDM, UCIHAR, the MNIST-1D negation example, and the retained many-to-one settings. New diagnostics use existing datasets. Computer vision and foundation-model extensions are proposed future work, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds frozen-random-factor comparators, labeled LoRA-FF at ranks 2, 4, 8, and 16 and LoKrA-FF, against SFT in Figures 13–15. This extends the existing PEFT comparison family while retaining the original SFDA and PEFT comparators.

E3.justification: New experiments compare training both PEFT factors with freezing the randomly initialized factor, and track source empirical risk before decomposition and through recovery epochs 0–3. Existing dataset splits, target sample fractions, rank factors, and learning-rate searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds source-loss recovery analysis in Figure 11 and a frozen-factor PEFT ablation across SSC, HHAR, and MFD in Figures 13–15. These test whether recovery training restores source behavior and whether fixed random adaptation subspaces suffice, substantially extending the diagnostic evidence. Existing subspace and hybrid-tuning ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions with different random seeds and retain the same tabulated uncertainty and plotted uncertainty conventions. v2 introduces no new run-count policy, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds source-risk recovery trajectories, and Figures 13–15 add extensive F1 results for frozen-factor PEFT variants across methods, ranks, and sample fractions. Retained numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged; v2 Table 14 reproduces v1 Table 2. These are additional findings, not improved scores for the unchanged SFT experiments.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 derives forward and backward equivalence between composed and factorized weights and gives gradients for the individual factors. The PAC-Bayesian theorem, parameter-distance lemmas, assumptions, and their proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient Tucker-based source preparation, selective adaptation, implicit regularization, compatibility with existing SFDA methods, and substantial parameter and MAC reductions.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing frozen-factor underperformance to arbitrary subspace constraints and expands the motivation connecting channel redundancy with time-series dependencies. It also clarifies the explanatory role of established PAC-Bayesian theory and discusses untested extensions. The fixed-rank and factor-interpretability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.8 substantially expands implementation documentation beyond v1's brief method summaries: it specifies adaptation losses, SHOT pseudo-label and centroid updates, NRC/AAD memory-bank operations, and the frozen MAPU imputer. These are newly documented details rather than established changes to the existing experiments.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.12 substantially broadens research positioning, including comparisons with Monarch and block tensor train parameterizations, foundation-model-assisted adaptation, and time-series foundation models. Section 2 also adds recent time-series adaptation references and a fuller Tucker-versus-CP rationale. These additions are discussions, not evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The appendix receives extensive explanatory expansion and organization into dedicated computational-example, propagation-equivalence, adaptation-objective, extended-related-work, and future-work sections. The main narrative remains largely intact, with local wording, notation, cross-reference, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds four diagnostic figures and substantially restructures the main tables for readability. Table 1 becomes a larger SSC-only display, with other results retained in Table 4; Table 2 shows two settings, while its complete predecessor appears as Table 14. Existing figures are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves support and clarity through recovery measurements, frozen-factor controls, explicit adaptation details, and more readable main tables without removing earlier evidence. These gains strengthen understanding of the existing framework rather than resolving a fundamental methodological deficiency. The added interpretation of frozen-factor underperformance remains broader than the mixed comparisons in Figures 14–15, limiting the strength of that explanatory gain.
